domain: antimicrobial resistance outbreak in a hospital

Carbapenem-resistant enterobacteria.provides: silent carriage for months, spread by hands and by sinks, very few treatment options

Meticillin-resistant staphylococcus.provides: decolonisation possible, spread by direct contact, established screening exists

Clostridioides difficile.provides: spore survival on surfaces for months, defeated only by sporicidal cleaning

Multi-resistant fungal species.provides: survival of routine disinfection, no decolonisation regimen at all

Hands of staff.requires: direct contact between patient and staff
Hands of staff.provides: interruptible by hand hygiene alone, the commonest route by far

Contaminated environment and equipment.provides: independent of any individual staff behaviour, reservoir persisting between patients

Wastewater plumbing.requires: sink traps and drains harbouring biofilm
Wastewater plumbing.provides: continuous reintroduction, no cleaning regimen reaching it, engineering works required

Patient transfer between units.provides: seeding of a new ward, detectable by admission screening

Hand hygiene campaign.provides: reduction of contact spread, no effect on an environmental reservoir

Contact precautions and isolation.requires: single rooms and enough of them
Contact precautions and isolation.provides: separation of colonised patients, limited by room availability

Sporicidal terminal cleaning.requires: an agent active against spores and time to apply it
Sporicidal terminal cleaning.provides: removal of surface reservoir, no effect on carriage in a patient

Antimicrobial stewardship.provides: reduction of selection pressure over months, no effect on transmission already under way

Ward outbreak controlled.provides: ward closure and deep clean, no wider spread

Hospital-wide endemic spread.provides: permanent screening burden, elective activity constrained

Unit closure to admissions.provides: loss of capacity, transfer of pressure to other hospitals
